newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan ends up at two-year high vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan ends up at two-year high vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at a two-year high close of 8.2917 against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday in Shanghai, from Monday's 8.2922, with buying active at the 8.2920 level due to strong pro-yuan sentiment, traders said.
The close was the highest since May 18, 1995 when the yuan ended at 8.2895.
The weighted average price on Monday was 8.2923.

The yuan opened slightly down at an intraday low of 8.2923 and rose to move mostly in a range between 8.2916 and 8.2920 during trading, hitting a high of 8.2911. Trading was dull with most business done at 8.2918, traders said.
One dealer said the yuan had gained strong upward momentum after a technical correction on Monday.
"The yuan opened lower, but active buying was seen at about 8.2920, which pushed it up by the close," he said.
A second dealer said the buying indicated the yuan had found its bottom at around the 8.2920 level.
"If there is no major negative news, the yuan is expected to continue to rise in the short term," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to test the key 8.2900 resistance level on Wednesday.

The yuan closed down at 7.2830 from 7.1520 against 100 Japanese yen due to the yen's strong performance on the world market, traders said. It closed down at an intraday low of 1.0723 from 1.0718 against the Hong Kong dollar.
